# OpenArtha

OpenArtha is an open, source-aware library for finding meaning in primary texts by reading the text, comparing interpretations, and following every reading to its source. Artha (AR-tha) means meaning, purpose, or sense in Sanskrit. The Bhagavad Gita is the first work.

Current corpus: gita-1.0.0-rc.1
Status: research preview; two independent human reviews are pending for every passage.
Contents: 18 chapters, 700 canonical passages, Devanagari Sanskrit, IAST, a provisional verse-aligned K. T. Telang English translation, variants, provenance, and SHA-256 checksums.
Commentary corpus: gita-commentaries-0.2.0 research preview, with all 29 supplied Sanskrit, English, and Hindi translation/commentary fields from 22 authors published under the pinned source snapshot's GPL-3.0 terms.

Human-readable entry points:
- /gita — chapter index and corpus search
- /gita/commentaries — Gita commentary registry and author-by-chapter reading
- /sources — bibliography and rights
- /data — immutable TEI XML, JSONL, and CSV downloads
- /methodology — recension, validation, review, and versioning method

Read-only APIs:
- /api/v1/works
- /api/v1/passages/gita/{chapter}/{verse}
- /api/v1/search?q={query}
- /api/v1/sources
- /api/v1/corpus-versions
- /api/v2/search?q={query} — unified root, translation, and commentary search
- /api/v2/passages/gita/{chapter}/{verse} — root passage with public commentaries
- /api/v2/commentaries/authors — compatibility registry endpoint for the Gita
- /api/v1/works/gita/passages/{chapter}/{verse} — text-scoped Gita passage
- /api/v1/works/gita/search?q={query} — text-scoped root-text search
- /api/v1/works/gita/sources — text-scoped sources
- /api/v1/works/gita/versions — text-scoped release versions
- /api/v2/works/gita/passages/{chapter}/{verse} — text-scoped Gita passage with commentary
- /api/v2/works/gita/search?q={query} — text-scoped unified Gita search

API responses are JSON by default. Request Accept: text/markdown or add ?format=markdown for Markdown.
Do not describe this release candidate as a fully human-verified edition.
Search is intentionally scoped to one work; do not infer cross-work search from a Gita result.
Do not describe machine-aligned commentary records as independently human-verified.
